dataset.description:
EU-SILC microdata provide harmonised, high-quality information on household income, poverty, social exclusion, living conditions, and labour market participation across all EU Member States. The dataset contains detailed person- and household-level variables on demographics, employment status, earnings, education, housing conditions, health, and material deprivation, enabling comprehensive distributional and inequality analyses.  
For this project, EU-SILC microdata serve as a key source for examining differences in labour market outcomes and income dynamics across population groups, with a particular focus on gender disparities. The dataset allows the project team to identify the determinants of the gender pay gap in Europe, assess how wage inequalities evolved during and after the Covid-19 crisis, and quantify the contribution of individual, household, and labour market characteristics to these disparities. 
EU-SILC’s harmonised structure enables robust cross-country comparisons and supports the development of aggregated analytical indicators used in the project’s scientific publications, working papers, and policy reports. All analyses are conducted using anonymised microdata made available under Eurostat’s strict confidentiality and secure access procedures.

dmp.description:
This document is the initial version of the Data Management Plan (DMP) for the research study (2025–2027), conducted within the Fundamental and Applied Research Programme under project No. LZP-2024/1-0616, "StAR: Labour Market Response to Shocks – Strategies for Adaptability and Resilience." The DMP will be managed as a living document using the Argos DMP tool, with significant updates periodically uploaded to Zenodo throughout the project's duration. Regular revisions will align with periodic project evaluations, or more frequently as necessary.

The DMP outlines a comprehensive strategy for managing the data used during the StAR project. The project aims to advance scientific understanding of how labour markets respond to major economic shocks, with a specific focus on the Financial Recession, the Covid-19 pandemic, and the surge in energy prices following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. It also examines the determinants and evolution of the gender pay gap in Europe, the long-term effects of job displacement in Latvia, and the link between unemployment and transitions into entrepreneurship. In addition, the project investigates the role of firms and job mobility in shaping gender wage disparities in Latvia. 

The StAR project relies exclusively on secondary, anonymised datasets accessed under strict confidentiality and legal agreements. These include harmonised microdata from EU-SILC and the Labour Force Survey for all EU Member States, Eurostat sector-level productivity statistics, matched employer-employee (MEE) administrative records compiled by the State Revenue Service (SRS) and managed by the Central Statistical Bureau (CSB). These datasets allow for detailed analysis, while all processing of confidential microdata is carried out on CSB’s secure remote servers. 

The final research outputs will include policy reports presenting evidence-based, context-sensitive recommendations, alongside scientific publications, working papers, and policy briefs. Together, these outputs will support informed decision-making by policymakers and other stakeholders in Latvia and the wider European context.
